A cleaning service charges a fee for each office and for each home. Last month, the number of offices cleaned, $f$, and the number of homes cleaned, $h$, was at most 14. Which inequality represents this situation?

A. $f + h \le 14$
B. $f + h \ge 14$
C. $f - h \le 14$
D. $f - h \ge 14$

Monarch butterflies can only fly when their body temperature is at least $55.0^\circ$F. If a monarch butterfly's current body temperature is $51.3^\circ$F, by at least how many degrees Fahrenheit must its body temperature increase before it can fly?

A. 1.3
B. 3.7
C. 5.0
D. 6.3

Maria rents a boat. She pays a fee of $\$60$ per hour and a $\$10$ fee for the course she chooses. She has no more than $\$280$ to spend. What is the maximum number of whole hours Maria can rent the boat?

The perimeter of a rectangle is at most 27 inches. The inequality $2\ell + 2w \le 27$ represents this situation, where $\ell$ is the length and $w$ is the width of the rectangle. Which statement is the best interpretation of $(\ell, w) = (8, 3)$ in this context?

A. A rectangle with a length of 8 inches and a width of 3 inches has a perimeter of at most 27 inches.
B. A rectangle with a length of 8 inches and a width of 3 inches has a perimeter of exactly 27 inches.
C. A rectangle with a length of 8 inches and a width of 3 inches has a perimeter of at least 27 inches.
D. A rectangle with a length of 8 inches and a width of 3 inches does not have a perimeter of at most 27 inches.

A geologist has a collection of rocks that are all the same type and estimates that each rock weighs about 165 pounds per cubic foot. The geologist calculates that the volume of each rock is between 12.7 cubic feet and 15.7 cubic feet, inclusive. Which inequality represents all possible weights $w$, in pounds, of a rock in this collection?

A. $12.7 \le w \le 15.7$
B. $165 \le w \le 177.7$
C. $177.7 \le w \le 180.7$
D. $2{,}095.5 \le w \le 2{,}590.5$

A teacher is ordering workbooks and flash cards for her students. Workbooks cost $\$3$ each and flash cards cost $\$4$ each. She wants to order at least 20 items and spend at most $\$80$. Which system of inequalities represents this situation, where $x$ represents the number of workbooks and $y$ represents the number of flash cards?

A. $x + y \ge 20$ and $3x + 4y \le 80$
B. $x + y \ge 20$ and $3x + 4y \ge 80$
C. $x + y \le 20$ and $3x + 4y \le 80$
D. $x + y \le 20$ and $3x + 4y \ge 80$

During a 3-week period, the temperature in a certain city ranged from $31^\circ$F to $67^\circ$F, inclusive. Which inequality represents all possible temperatures $t$, in degrees Fahrenheit, during this 3-week period?

A. $|t - 31| \le 67$
B. $|t + 31| \le 67$
C. $|t - 49| \le 18$
D. $|t + 49| \le 18$

[Graph showing a coordinate plane with a solid boundary line passing through $(0, -6)$ and $(9, 0)$, with the region above the line shaded.]

Which inequality represents the shaded region shown?

A. $y \ge \frac{2}{3}x - 6$
B. $y \le \frac{2}{3}x - 6$
C. $y \ge \frac{3}{2}x - 6$
D. $y \le \frac{3}{2}x - 6$

A clothing store is having a sale on shirts and pants. The shirts cost $\$15$ each and the pants cost $\$25$ each. A customer wants to spend at most $\$120$. Which inequality represents this situation, where $s$ is the number of shirts and $p$ is the number of pants the customer can buy?

A. $15s + 25p \le 120$
B. $15s + 25p \ge 120$
C. $15s - 25p \le 120$
D. $15s - 25p \ge 120$

Which of the following ordered pairs $(x, y)$ satisfies the inequality $5x - 3y < 4$?

I. $(0, 0)$
II. $(2, 3)$
III. $(-2, -4)$

A. I only
B. I and II only
C. II and III only
D. I, II, and III

According to one study, a person's normal body temperature can range from $97.8^\circ$F to $99.0^\circ$F, inclusive. Which of the following could be Kevin's normal body temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit?

A. 96.3
B. 97.0
C. 98.2
D. 99.5

[Graph showing a coordinate plane with a dashed boundary line and a shaded region.]

Which ordered pair is a solution to the inequality shown in the graph?

A. $(0, -4)$
B. $(0, 4)$
C. $(-4, 0)$
D. $(4, 0)$

A geologist needs to collect at least 67 samples of lava from a certain volcano. The geologist has already collected 63 samples. How many more samples does the geologist need to collect to meet the minimum requirement?

A. At least 4
B. At most 4
C. At least 130
D. At most 130
A party planner needs at least 50 dinner rolls for a party. Dinner rolls come in packages of 12. What is the minimum number of packages the party planner should buy?

Dragonflies can travel anywhere from 1,510 miles to 4,130 miles during migration. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible distances $d$, in miles, a dragonfly can travel during migration?

A. $d \le 1{,}510$
B. $d \ge 4{,}130$
C. $1{,}510 \le d \le 4{,}130$
D. $d \le 1{,}510$ or $d \ge 4{,}130$

Tom scored 85, 78, and 98 on three tests. Which inequality can be used to find the score $G$ he must earn on the fourth test so that his average test score is at least 90?

A. $\frac{85 + 78 + 98}{3} + G \ge 90$
B. $\frac{85 + 78 + 98 + G}{4} \ge 90$
C. $\frac{85 + 78 + 98 + G}{4} \le 90$
D. $\frac{G}{4} + 85 + 78 + 98 \ge 90$

Ty walks at a speed of 4 kilometers per hour. He has a goal of walking at least 24 kilometers. What is the minimum number of hours Ty must walk to meet his goal?

A. 4
B. 6
C. 20
D. 28

Julissa needs at least 100 flight hours to earn her pilot's license. She has already completed 86 flight hours. What is the minimum number of additional flight hours she needs to complete?

A. 14
B. 86
C. 100
D. 186

A bakery uses trays to hold baked goods. Each tray can hold anywhere from 50 to 60 cookies. If the bakery uses 4 trays, which of the following could be the total number of cookies?

A. 180
B. 200
C. 220
D. 260

Rhett drives at an average speed of 35 miles per hour for $r$ hours and Jessica drives at an average speed of 40 miles per hour for $j$ hours. Their combined distance driven is under 220 miles. Which inequality represents this situation?

A. $35r + 40j < 220$
B. $35r + 40j > 220$
C. $35r + 40j \le 220$
D. $35r + 40j \ge 220$

A surf shop rents surfboards. There is a $\$25$ service fee plus a rental rate of $\$10$ per hour. A person wants to spend at most $\$75$ on surfboard rental. Which inequality represents this situation, where $t$ is the time, in hours, of the rental?

A. $25 + 10t \le 75$
B. $25 + 10t \ge 75$
C. $25t + 10 \le 75$
D. $25t + 10 \ge 75$

Two containers hold beads. One container holds beads that are 30% red and the other holds beads that are 70% red. If $x$ beads are taken from the first container and $y$ beads are taken from the second container, the total number of red beads must be at least 400. Which inequality represents this situation?

A. $0.3x + 0.7y \ge 400$
B. $0.3x + 0.7y \le 400$
C. $0.7x + 0.3y \ge 400$
D. $0.7x + 0.3y \le 400$

An airplane's cruising speed ranges from 150 to 170 miles per hour, inclusive. Which inequality represents all possible cruising speeds $s$, in miles per hour, of the airplane?

A. $s \le 150$
B. $s \ge 170$
C. $150 \le s \le 170$
D. $s \le 150$ or $s \ge 170$

The point $(8, 2)$ is a solution to which of the following systems of inequalities?

A. $x > 0$ and $y > 0$
B. $x > 0$ and $y < 0$
C. $x < 0$ and $y > 0$
D. $x < 0$ and $y < 0$

$$y \le 3x + 1$$
$$x - y > 1$$

Which ordered pair is a solution to the system of inequalities above?

A. $(-2, -1)$
B. $(-1, 3)$
C. $(1, 5)$
D. $(2, -1)$

[Graph showing a coordinate plane with a dashed boundary line passing through $(0, 1)$ and $(1, -3)$ with slope $-4$. The region above the line is shaded.]

Which inequality represents the shaded region shown?

A. $y > 1 - 4x$
B. $y < 1 - 4x$
C. $y > 4x + 1$
D. $y < 4x + 1$

The minimum value of $x$ is 12 less than 6 times the value of $n$. Which inequality shows the possible values of $x$?

A. $x \le 6n - 12$
B. $x \ge 6n - 12$
C. $x \le 12 - 6n$
D. $x \ge 12 - 6n$

A homeowner uses a certain type of heating system that costs $\$4{,}334$ annually. The homeowner plans to switch to a geothermal heating system, which costs $\$2{,}712$ annually, but the installation costs $\$25{,}000$. After how many years will the savings from using the geothermal heating system exceed the installation cost?

A. 9
B. 15
C. 16
D. 17

A truck is towing a trailer that weighs 500 pounds. The truck can tow a maximum of 4,600 pounds. Boxes weighing 120 pounds each will be loaded onto the trailer. What is the maximum number of boxes that can be loaded onto the trailer while it is being towed by the truck?

A. 4
B. 5
C. 34
D. 38

Some types of whales can travel 72 to 77 miles per day. If a group of whales travels at this rate for 16 days, which of the following inequalities represents all possible values of the total distance $x$, in miles, the whales could travel?

A. $72 \le x \le 77$
B. $88 \le x \le 93$
C. $(72)(16) \le x \le (77)(16)$
D. $\frac{72}{16} \le x \le \frac{77}{16}$

An event planner is planning a party. The cost of the venue is $\$35$ and the cost of food is $\$10.25$ per attendee. The event planner has a budget of $\$200$. What is the maximum number of attendees the event planner can have at the party?

A rectangle has a length of 50 and a width of $x$. The perimeter of the rectangle is at most 210. Which inequality represents this situation?

A. $2x + 100 \le 210$
B. $2x + 100 \ge 210$
C. $50x \le 210$
D. $50x \ge 210$

A homeowner wants to plant azaleas and boxwoods in a garden. The homeowner can plant at most 164 plants total. The number of azaleas must be no more than 3 times the number of boxwoods. Which system of inequalities represents this situation, where $a$ is the number of azaleas and $b$ is the number of boxwoods?

A. $a + b \le 164$ and $a \le 3b$
B. $a + b \ge 164$ and $a \le 3b$
C. $a + b \le 164$ and $a \ge 3b$
D. $a + b \ge 164$ and $a \ge 3b$

A botanist found that a certain tall plant species has heights ranging from 106 cm to 158 cm. A plant is classified as tall if its height is more than 100 cm. Which of the following inequalities is the most accurate representation of the possible heights $h$, in cm, of the plants in the tall plant species?

A. $h > 100$
B. $106 \le h \le 158$
C. $100 < h \le 158$
D. $h \ge 106$

$$y > 14$$
$$4x + y < 18$$

A point $(x, 53)$ is a solution to the system of inequalities above. Which of the following could be the value of $x$?

A. $-16$
B. $-9$
C. 9
D. 16

$$y > 4x + 8$$

Which of the following tables gives values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $y$ that are all solutions to the given inequality?

A. $x = 2, y = 14$; $x = 4, y = 22$; $x = 6, y = 30$
B. $x = 2, y = 16$; $x = 4, y = 26$; $x = 6, y = 36$
C. $x = 2, y = 18$; $x = 4, y = 28$; $x = 6, y = 38$
D. $x = 2, y = 20$; $x = 4, y = 30$; $x = 6, y = 40$

[Graph showing a coordinate plane with a dashed boundary line passing through $(0, -1)$ and $(1, -4)$ with slope $-3$. The region above the line is shaded.]

Which inequality represents the shaded region shown?

A. $y > -1 - 3x$
B. $y < -1 - 3x$
C. $y > -3 - x$
D. $y < -3 - x$

$$y > 7x - 4$$

Which of the following tables gives values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $y$ that are all solutions to the given inequality?

A. $x = 3, y = 15$; $x = 5, y = 29$; $x = 8, y = 50$
B. $x = 3, y = 17$; $x = 5, y = 31$; $x = 8, y = 52$
C. $x = 3, y = 19$; $x = 5, y = 33$; $x = 8, y = 56$
D. $x = 3, y = 21$; $x = 5, y = 35$; $x = 8, y = 58$

$$y < x$$
$$x < 22$$

Which of the following tables gives values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $y$ that are all solutions to the given system of inequalities?

A. $x = 19, y = 20$; $x = 20, y = 21$; $x = 21, y = 22$
B. $x = 19, y = 18$; $x = 20, y = 19$; $x = 21, y = 20$
C. $x = 22, y = 21$; $x = 23, y = 22$; $x = 24, y = 23$
D. $x = 22, y = 23$; $x = 23, y = 24$; $x = 24, y = 25$
A value of $x$ is at most 17 less than 5 times the value of $y$. If the value of $y$ is 3, what is the greatest possible value of $x$?

The Karvonen formula gives a person's target heart rate $H$, in beats per minute, during exercise as $H = 120p + 60$, where $p$ is a number between 0.5 and 0.85, inclusive. Which of the following inequalities gives all the possible values of the target heart rate $H$ according to this formula?

A. $60 \le H \le 120$
B. $80 \le H \le 120$
C. $120 \le H \le 162$
D. $80 \le H \le 162$

An event planner is planning a party. The cost of the venue is $\$35$ and the cost of food is $\$10.25$ per attendee. The event planner has a budget of $\$300$. What is the maximum number of attendees the event planner can have at the party?

An elephant weighs 200 pounds at birth. It gains between 2 and 3 pounds per day for the first 365 days. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible weights $w$, in pounds, of an elephant that is at most 365 days old?

A. $200 \le w \le 365$
B. $202 \le w \le 203$
C. $400 \le w \le 565$
D. $930 \le w \le 1{,}295$

$$y < -4x + 4$$

Which point $(x, y)$ is a solution to the given inequality?

A. $(-4, 0)$
B. $(0, 4)$
C. $(0, 8)$
D. $(4, 0)$

A truck can haul a maximum of 5,630 pounds. A piece of equipment that weighs 190 pounds is already on the truck. Crates that weigh either 25 pounds or 62 pounds each will be loaded on the truck. Which inequality represents this situation, where $x$ is the number of 25-pound crates and $y$ is the number of 62-pound crates that can be loaded on the truck?

A. $25x + 62y \le 5{,}440$
B. $25x + 62y \ge 5{,}440$
C. $25x + 62y \le 5{,}630$
D. $25x + 62y \ge 5{,}630$

$$y \le x$$
$$y \le -x$$

Which of the following ordered pairs $(x, y)$ is a solution to the system of inequalities above?

A. $(-1, 0)$
B. $(0, -1)$
C. $(0, 1)$
D. $(1, 0)$

[Graph showing a coordinate plane with a shaded region bounded by inequalities.]

Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the system of inequalities shown in the graph?

A. $(-4, -2)$
B. $(0, 6)$
C. $(6, -2)$
D. $(6, 6)$

A parking lot has spaces that range from 7.5 feet to 9.0 feet wide. A curb is 135 feet long. What is the range of the number of parking spaces $n$ that can fit along the curb?

A. $7.5 \le n \le 9.0$
B. $15 \le n \le 18$
C. $126 \le n \le 144$
D. $145.5 \le n \le 150$

A weather forecaster reports that the snowfall rate is between 0.6 inches per hour and 1.8 inches per hour. Which inequality represents all possible values of the snowfall rate $s$, in inches per hour?

A. $s \le 0.6$
B. $s \ge 1.8$
C. $0.6 \le s \le 1.8$
D. $s \le 0.6$ or $s \ge 1.8$

$$2x - y > 883$$

Which of the following tables gives values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $y$ that are all solutions to the given inequality?

A. $x = 440, y = -4$; $x = 441, y = -2$; $x = 442, y = 0$
B. $x = 440, y = -5$; $x = 441, y = -3$; $x = 442, y = -1$
C. $x = 440, y = -3$; $x = 441, y = 0$; $x = 442, y = 2$
D. $x = 440, y = -2$; $x = 441, y = 0$; $x = 442, y = 2$

A helicopter can carry a combination of 100-pound packages and 120-pound packages. The helicopter must carry at least 10 packages total and can carry a maximum total weight of 1,100 pounds. What is the maximum number of 120-pound packages the helicopter can carry?

A. 3
B. 4
C. 5
D. 9

$$y > 2x - 1$$
$$2x > 5$$

Which of the following consists of the $y$-coordinates of all the points that satisfy the system of inequalities above?

A. $y > 6$
B. $y > 4$
C. $y > \frac{5}{2}$
D. $y > \frac{3}{2}$

Ken is working this summer as part of a crew on a farm. He earned $\$8$ per hour for the first 10 hours he worked this week. Because of his performance, his crew leader raised his salary to $\$10$ per hour for the rest of the week. Ken saves 90% of his earnings from each week. What is the least number of hours he must work the rest of the week to save at least $\$270$ for the week?

A. 38
B. 33
C. 22
D. 16

$$11x + 14y \le 115$$

Anthony will spend at most $\$115$ to purchase $x$ small cheese pizzas and $y$ large cheese pizzas for a team dinner. The given inequality represents this situation. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $14y$ in this context?

A. The amount, in dollars, Anthony will spend on each large cheese pizza
B. The amount, in dollars, Anthony will spend on each small cheese pizza
C. The total amount, in dollars, Anthony will spend on large cheese pizzas
D. The total amount, in dollars, Anthony will spend on small cheese pizzas

In a set of four consecutive odd integers, where the integers are ordered from least to greatest, the first integer is represented by $x$. The product of 12 and the fourth odd integer is at most 26 less than the sum of the first and third odd integers. Which inequality represents this situation?

A. $12(x + 6) \le x + (x + 4) - 26$
B. $12(x + 6) \ge 26 - (x + (x + 4))$
C. $12(x + 4) \le x + (x + 3) - 26$
D. $12(x + 4) \ge 26 - (x + (x + 3))$

A business owner plans to purchase the same model of chair for each of the 81 employees. The total budget to spend on these chairs is $\$14{,}000$, which includes a 7% sales tax. Which of the following is closest to the maximum possible price per chair, before sales tax, the business owner could pay based on this budget?

A. $\$148.15$
B. $\$161.53$
C. $\$172.84$
D. $\$184.94$

$$y < 6x + 2$$

For which of the following tables are all the values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $y$ solutions to the given inequality?

A. $x = 3, y = 20$; $x = 5, y = 32$; $x = 7, y = 44$
B. $x = 3, y = 16$; $x = 5, y = 36$; $x = 7, y = 40$
C. $x = 3, y = 16$; $x = 5, y = 28$; $x = 7, y = 40$
D. $x = 3, y = 24$; $x = 5, y = 36$; $x = 7, y = 48$

A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 130 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 60 inches and its length is 2.5 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width $x$, in inches, of the box?

A. $0 < x \le 10$
B. $0 < x \le 11\frac{2}{3}$
C. $0 < x \le 17\frac{1}{2}$
D. $0 < x \le 20$

$$y > 13x - 18$$

For which of the following tables are all the values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $y$ solutions to the given inequality?

A. $x = 3, y = 21$; $x = 5, y = 47$; $x = 8, y = 86$
B. $x = 3, y = 26$; $x = 5, y = 42$; $x = 8, y = 86$
C. $x = 3, y = 16$; $x = 5, y = 42$; $x = 8, y = 81$
D. $x = 3, y = 26$; $x = 5, y = 52$; $x = 8, y = 91$

$$I = \frac{V}{R}$$

The formula above is Ohm's law for an electric circuit with current $I$, in amperes, potential difference $V$, in volts, and resistance $R$, in ohms. A circuit has a resistance of 500 ohms, and its potential difference will be generated by $n$ six-volt batteries that produce a total potential difference of $6n$ volts. If the circuit is to have a current of no more than 0.25 ampere, what is the greatest number, $n$, of six-volt batteries that can be used?

The triangle inequality theorem states that the sum of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the length of the third side. If a triangle has side lengths of 6 and 12, which inequality represents the possible lengths, $x$, of the third side of the triangle?

A. $x < 18$
B. $x > 18$
C. $6 < x < 18$
D. $x < 6$ or $x > 18$

$$y < 5x + 6$$

For which of the following tables are all the values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $y$ solutions to the given inequality?

A. $x = 3, y = 17$; $x = 5, y = 27$; $x = 7, y = 37$
B. $x = 3, y = 17$; $x = 5, y = 35$; $x = 7, y = 37$
C. $x = 3, y = 25$; $x = 5, y = 35$; $x = 7, y = 45$
D. $x = 3, y = 21$; $x = 5, y = 31$; $x = 7, y = 41$

A team hosting an event to raise money for new uniforms plans to sell at least 140 tickets before this event and at least 220 tickets during this event to raise a total of at least $\$5{,}820$ from all tickets sold. The price of a ticket during this event is $\$3$ less than the price of a ticket before this event. Which inequality represents this situation, where $x$ is the price, in dollars, of a ticket sold during this event?

A. $140(x + 3) + 220x \le 5{,}820$
B. $140(x + 3) + 220x \ge 5{,}820$
C. $140(x - 3) + 220x \le 5{,}820$
D. $140(x - 3) + 220x \ge 5{,}820$

A small business owner budgets $\$2{,}200$ to purchase candles. The owner must purchase a minimum of 200 candles to maintain the discounted pricing. If the owner pays $\$4.90$ per candle to purchase small candles and $\$11.60$ per candle to purchase large candles, what is the maximum number of large candles the owner can purchase to stay within the budget and maintain the discounted pricing?
A number $x$ is at most 2 less than 3 times the value of $y$. If the value of $y$ is $-4$, what is the greatest possible value of $x$?

A salesperson's total earnings consist of a base salary of $x$ dollars per year, plus commission earnings of 11% of the total sales the salesperson makes during the year. This year, the salesperson has a goal for the total earnings to be at least 3 times and at most 4 times the base salary. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible values of total sales $s$, in dollars, the salesperson can make this year in order to meet their goal?

A. $2x \le s \le 3x$
B. $\frac{2}{0.11}x \le s \le \frac{3}{0.11}x$
C. $3x \le s \le 4x$
D. $\frac{3}{0.11}x \le s \le \frac{4}{0.11}x$

$$y \le x + 7$$
$$y \ge -2x - 1$$

Which point $(x, y)$ is a solution to the given system of inequalities in the $xy$-plane?

A. $(-14, 0)$
B. $(0, -14)$
C. $(0, 14)$
D. $(14, 0)$

A local transit company sells a monthly pass for $\$95$ that allows an unlimited number of trips of any length. Tickets for individual trips cost $\$1.50$, $\$2.50$, or $\$3.50$, depending on the length of the trip. What is the minimum number of trips per month for which a monthly pass could cost less than purchasing individual tickets for trips?

Adam's school is a 20-minute walk or a 5-minute bus ride away from his house. The bus runs once every 30 minutes, and the number of minutes, $w$, that Adam waits for the bus varies between 0 and 30. Which of the following inequalities gives the values of $w$ for which it would be faster for Adam to walk to school?

A. $w - 5 < 20$
B. $w - 5 > 20$
C. $w + 5 < 20$
D. $w + 5 > 20$

The members of a city council wanted to assess the opinions of all city residents
about converting an open field into a dog park. The council surveyed a sample of
500 city residents who own dogs. The survey showed that the majority of those
sampled were in favor of the dog park. Which of the following is true about the city
council’s survey?
A. It shows that the majority of city residents are in favor of the dog park.
B. The survey sample should have included more residents who are dog owners.
C. The survey sample should have consisted entirely of residents who do not own dogs.
D. The survey sample is biased because it is not representative of all city residents.

A market researcher selected 200 people at random from a group of people who
indicated that they liked a certain book. The 200 people were shown a movie based on
the book and then asked whether they liked or disliked the movie. Of those surveyed,
95% said they disliked the movie. Which of the following inferences can appropriately
be drawn from this survey result?
A. At least 95% of people who go see movies will dislike this movie.
B. At least 95% of people who read books will dislike this movie.
C. Most people who dislike this book will like this movie.
D. Most people who like this book will dislike this movie.

Residents of a town were surveyed to determine whether they are satisfied with the
concession stand at the local park. A random sample of 200 residents was selected.
All 200 responded, and 87% said they are satisfied. Based on this information, which of
the following statements must be true?
I. Of all the town residents, 87% would say they are satisfied with the concession stand at the local park.
II. If another random sample of 200 residents were surveyed, 87% would say they are satisfied.
A. Neither
B. I only
C. II only
D. I and II

A survey was conducted using a sample of history professors selected at random from
the California State Universities. The professors surveyed were asked to name the
publishers of their current texts. What is the largest population to which the results of
the survey can be generalized?
A. All professors in the United States
B. All history professors in the United States
C. All history professors at all California State Universities
D. All professors at all California State Universities

A polling agency recently surveyed 1,000 adults who were selected at random from a
large city and asked each of the adults, “Are you satisfied with the quality of air in the
city?” Of those surveyed, 78 percent responded that they were satisfied with the quality
